newsitem.title: GERMANY: New Siemens software helps automation sales.
newsitem.headline: New Siemens software helps automation sales.

text.p: German industrial giant Siemens AG said on Wednesday it expected a newly developed software system to spur dramatic growth in sales to customers looking to streamline their production processes.

The system should lift sales of manufacturing and process automation systems by 60 percent over the next five years, Manfred von Raven, general manager of Siemens automation technology unit, said in a statement.
Sales of "Totally Integrated Automation" systems should also nearly double Siemens' share of the worldwide process automation market to 20 percent, von Raven said.

Process automation systems generated 20 percent of the automation business' 6.6 billion marks sales in the 1995-96 business year, he said. Sales were down four percent from 1994-95, but pre-tax profit rose 22 percent to 509 billion marks, making the unit one of Siemens' most profitable.
At the heart of the new automation system is a standard software platform that can be modified to manage a wide variety of manufacturing processes, von Raven said.
Installing a Totally Integrated Automation system will cost much less than using competing products, and should be able to serve customers over a period of 15 years, he said.
Siemens recently said it does not expect 1996-97 results to improve over those for the year that ended September 30. Previously, it had said it expected 20 percent growth for the next few years.
